sources.parts: By the model (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py), in oak: her hull is the dugout she was built on, 265 kg; her float, three metres of log hewn round to some 30 cm across, 224 L, 151 kg, and the three logs it is hewn from 3000 L before the first pass; her six poles (three crooked booms 9 cm across, a 3 m mast 9 cm across, two 3 m spars 7.5 cm), 118 L, 79 kg; her washstrakes, ten boards 2.5 cm thick, 41 L, 28 kg, as they are fitted. A float or poles of another wood weigh by their own
sources.swimmingOffsetY: Drawn at the draft she floats at with one aboard, 0.155 m (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py): vanilla floats a boat with the water 0.018 m over her selection box's top less this offset
sources.impactCapacity: The dugout's hull, in her hull's wood alone: the float and rig lashed to it take no knock a hull takes
sources.shell: The dugout's walls, about 5 cm thick, as the Dufuna canoe's (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dufuna_canoe)
sources.depthMetres: The dugout's, keel to gunwale: her washstrakes raise it by their stage's raisesMetres once sewn
sources.waterplaneSquareMetres: The dugout's 2.91 m² and her float's 0.86 m², a 3 m log 0.3 m wide at the water with hewn ends, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py); her three logs, before they are hewn, stand 3 m² at the water
sources.repairs: Her hull is a dugout's, mended as one

sources.time: A held action lasts the real time of that one piece of work over sixty: game time runs 30 times faster than real time, and boat work is halved again
sources.floatLogs: A small outrigger's float is about 3 m long
sources.floatOffMetres: A small outrigger's float rides 1.5 to 2 m off her hull: hull, gap, float, three blocks across
sources.floorMetres: The dugout's hold floor: her 0.5625 m rim less its 0.5125 m hollow
sources.booms: Setting one pole across her or up, about three minutes, as fitting one of a canoe's laths. A crooked pole, as Hawaiian and Marshallese booms curved down to the float (Young, 1876, marshall.csu.edu.au/Marshalls/html/culture/Canoes.html), takes its curve as it is laid: it rests on her gunwales and on the float's top, and settles with every pass as the float is hewn down beneath it
sources.hewing: Six passes of the axe all round take the three logs, 3000 L, down to the round float with pointed ends, 224 L (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py). Chip by chip, 463 L a pass, an axe biting some 0.08 L a stroke 30 times a minute (H. Glaser, physiology of forestry work, FAO): some three hours of real work a pass. A pass takes as long as vanilla takes to fell a large oak with a flint axe, 30 s (ItemAxe: a log's break time times the root of the tree's size)
sources.lashing: One rope is ten metres of lashing: about a quarter of an hour, as a canoe's (an estimate). Once the float is hewn, each boom is lashed to both gunwales and straight to the float, thirteen turns a lashing (ten round, three frapping) of their girth: 52 m, counted by her shape's builder
sources.sail: A crab claw of 3.5 m² between her two 3 m spars (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py), one cloth a square metre, as one linen block covers: four, each laced to the spars in about a quarter of an hour (an estimate)
sources.stays: A forestay, a backstay, a shroud out to the float and the sheet, each under ten metres: one rope each, set up in about a quarter of an hour (an estimate)
sources.strakes: Optional, any time she is finished: one washstrake a side between her solid ends, a board some 15 cm high, as Pacific washstrakes ran 15 to 20 cm (a Tikopia hull 43 cm deep carries a 15 cm one, Haddon & Hornell, Canoes of Oceania, via collections.maa.cam.ac.uk/objects/555827; Hawaiian mo'o 6 to 8 in). Sawn planks, a metre a plank: 8 along her sides, and a board across each end of her hollow, where her solid ends begin, as the end pieces lashed on at Tobi and Kapingamarangi (Haddon & Hornell; Buck 1950), so the sea cannot come in over her low ends: 10. Fitting one, with its row of holes, about twenty minutes (an estimate)
sources.seams: Sewn on through holes 3 in apart over a split batten (Haddon & Hornell, Mont-Dore canoe): each stitch about 30 cm of cord round wall, plank and batten, 116 stitches along her sides and her end boards, 35 m, four ropes (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py). Sewn, they raise her side 15 cm and add the 422 L of hold between them, her 2.81 m² opening 15 cm higher

sources.side: Her float lies 2 m off her starboard side as her model draws her, a hull turned end for end when rigged from the port: a knock from that side meets the float before her hull
sources.impactCapacity: As the raft's lashings, which take 1200 J in their three ropes, 40 J a metre: her booms are lashed to her gunwales and her float with 52 m of rope (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py), every turn of it between the float and her hull
sources.hull: What she was rigged on, left once her float comes away: the dugout
sources.keeps: What comes away whole with the float: her poles as they were laid, her sail's cloths, and her stays; her lashings part, and her washstrakes come off as the planks they were
sources.firewoodLitres: As the dugout breaks up: eight pieces of firewood from her 393 L of wood
sources.repairs: As the raft's: one and a half twines bind up a rope's worth of lashing, nine for her six ropes

sources.pushNewtons: A sustained two-handed push by an adult, about 300 N (Snook and Ciriello, 1991, maximum acceptable forces)
sources.friction: Wood sliding over wet sand or mud, about 0.4

sources.beamMetres: Hull and float apart: half the hull's 0.9 m, the float's 2 m out and half its 0.3 m
sources.mastMetres: A small outrigger's mast, about 3 m
sources.heave: As the dugout she is built on: her float adds a third to her waterplane and her rig half again to her weight, so she rises to a crest as slowly
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: The float spreads the craft to its whole beam: a breaker must be as high as hull and float apart to roll it
sources.rollResponse: The float's buoyancy and weight hold the hull upright: very steady in a sea
sources.pitchResponse: A long, narrow hull cuts through the swell rather than riding it

sources.capacityLitres: The dugout's hollow: her washstrakes add the 422 L they enclose once sewn (bin/lib/hulls/outrigger.py)
sources.deckSquareMetres: The dugout's opening at the rim catches the rain (bin/lib/hulls/dugout.py)
sources.drainLitresPerHour: One log, no seams: nothing leaks
